style: frustrated and blaming; blames the school, the dad and the child; run-on sentences

situations.name: Getting out the door for school in the morning
situations.feared_outcome: I'll throw up in class and everyone will see

behaviors.text: Lies on the floor by the front door, won't put shoes on, and stays home
Asks mom over and over what happens if he throws up, and whether she'll be home if he needs her

accommodations.text: Mom lets him stay home and calls the attendance office
Mom answers each what-if question every time he asks

situations.name: Mid-day at school with a stomachache

behaviors.text: Goes to the nurse with a stomachache and asks to call mom to be picked up

accommodations.text: Mom leaves work and picks him up early

situations.name: Friday spelling tests
situations.feared_outcome: I'll get words wrong and Mrs. Okafor will be mad at me

behaviors.text: Was off all morning on test day: quiet, barely ate
Asks mom in the car whether the teacher will be mad if he gets some wrong

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Lay on the floor by the front door and would not put his shoes on. Said he was going to puke at school.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I gave up after 20 min and let him stay home. Again. His dad was zero help, already gone to work like always.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Asked me probably 15 times what happens if he throws up in class. Did go in eventually.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Kept answering him, what else am I supposed to do, ignore him? Drove him.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Went to the nurse around 10 with a stomachache and asked to call me.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Left work and picked him up. Nurse said no fever. Third time this month and the school just keeps calling ME instead of dealing with it.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Was off all morning. Barely touched breakfast, didn't say a word in the car.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Told him it's just spelling and he needs to get over it.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Kept him home bc he was sobbing and I had a 9am I could not be late for. Called attendance.
monitoring_log.trap: parent action written in child field (keeping him home and calling attendance are the mom's actions, a1; the child's avoidance b1 is only implied)

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Made it till after lunch then went to the nurse wanting to go home.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Told the nurse no this time. He stayed. Cried apparently. His teacher could have handled it better honestly.

monitoring_log.parent_words: wednesday he got in the car fine then in the drop off line wouldnt get out, kept asking if Id be home all day in case he needed me. I said yes. he finally got out when the aide came over to the car. this is ridiculous for a 4th grader

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Went to school. In the car asked if Mrs. Okafor would be mad if he got some wrong.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Said no she won't be mad. Honestly I have no idea, she's pretty strict.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Said his stomach hurt, asked what if he pukes on the rug, asked if I'd have my phone on. Went in.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Answered him. Drove him, signed him in late at the office.

voice_notes.text: ok so this morning um he was up at like 6 and by 7:40 he's on the floor by the door again saying he's gonna throw up at school and i just i let him stay home i know i know but i had to be at work by 8:15 and his dad was no help so honestly id say he was at an 8 like full meltdown
voice_notes.trap: 7:40 and 8:15 are clock times and 6 is a wake-up time; only the 8 at the end is a fear level

voice_notes.text: two things today um first the nurse called again at like 11 he wanted to come home and i said no you have to stay and then at pickup he asked me like ten times if he has to go tomorrow and what if he throws up and i just kept saying yes you have to go no you wont throw up
voice_notes.trap: 11 is a time and ten is a count; no fear level was said
